questions.prompt: Let G be a simple undirected graph on n ≥ 2 vertices. Prove that if every vertex has degree at least (n−1)/2, then G is connected.

reference.answer: Proof by contradiction (or equivalent). Suppose G is disconnected. Let C be a connected component with the fewest vertices, |V(C)| = k. Then k ≤ n/2. Every vertex v ∈ C has all neighbors in C, so deg(v) ≤ k−1 ≤ n/2 − 1 = (n−2)/2 < (n−1)/2, contradicting the degree hypothesis. Hence G is connected.
key_ideas: Assume disconnected; pick a smallest component C
Deduce deg(v) ≤ |V(C)|−1 < (n−1)/2 for v in C

steps.description: Set up a correct proof strategy (e.g. contradiction via a component)
steps.expected: Clear plan: assume G disconnected and analyze a component (or equivalent valid approach).

steps.description: Obtain a size / degree bound on that component
steps.expected: Shows vertices in a proper component have deg ≤ |component|−1 and relates this to (n−1)/2.

steps.description: Reach a contradiction and conclude connectivity
steps.expected: Contradiction to δ(G) ≥ (n−1)/2; concludes G is connected.
